# Page-relative floating table alignment controls

These packages are manually authored XML, generated by
`tools/aligned_multipage_floating_fixture.py`. They use Arial, contain no font
programs or artwork, and do not reuse a corpus document or another engine.
Regenerate into a fresh directory with `--output-directory PATH`; compare the
DOCX hashes in the case manifests. Stable ZIP metadata makes all three packages
byte reproducible. Do not overwrite an already-open native source.

- `control.docx`: five 18-row tables, minimum row height 960 twips, across five
  next-page sections. Left, center, right, inside and outside horizontal
  positioning is relative to the margins; vertical positioning is numeric.
- `single-page.docx`: the same five positions with three rows per table.
- `single-page-parity.docx`: three-row inside/outside tables on both even- and
  odd-indexed pages. Distinct labels make every row identity unambiguous.

The reference application renders these sources on ten, five and four Letter pages.
The `*-reference.json` files retain declared text positions read with
`record_section_floating_native.py`. That reader removes FontFile references
before font construction and rejects glyph-program fallbacks. PDF/EMF programs
remain private; source and native PDF hashes bind the numeric references.
The owned-document capture preserves source bytes, Saved state, view, zoom and
selection. Open the exact source with the reference-opening helper before running
`tools/capture-owned-floating-reference.ps1` using Windows PowerShell
(`powershell.exe -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File ...`), with its matching manifest and a
fresh output directory. It never opens, saves, closes or quits reference application documents.

The single-page browser holdouts compare row identity, page and text origins;
their bounds are 0.35 pt horizontally and 0.15 pt vertically, including the
existing sub-point floating-frame difference. They cover editing every
inside/outside parity case, package preservation, exact undo, print stability
and editable reopening. These are bounded placement checks, not complete native
glyph, border or print-raster certification.

The multi-page source is now editable with supported horizontal positioning.
It retains all five tables and 90 row labels; no-edit/edit/export/reopen,
screen/print undo and both zooms are checked. The earlier import-only checkpoint
used read-only positioning recovery, described in its historical report.
`probe-aligned-multipage-floating.mjs` routes an isolated diagnostic which removes
only the horizontal layout guard, and a separate first-physical-page candidate.
After the importer fix, guard removal alone matches all 90 row
pages, but inside/outside origins differ by up to 251.396 pt. The reference application retains the
first fragment's horizontal side on its continuation page; using the following
anchor paragraph's final page is not a safe replacement. No guard-removal
candidate was shipped at that checkpoint. Vertical alignment and further
collision combinations remain open.

The absolute first-page diagnostic additionally uses the independent
`aligned-floating-parity-holdout` source across both page parities. It matches
162 row pages/origins within 0.31 pt X / 0.06 pt baseline across both controls.
That historical result did not enable production support. The later anchor,
initial-number and leading-flow checks now support horizontal aligned flow.
